actions.name: 上斜凳轻哑铃胸推
actions.phase: 45°上斜凳支撑下，双轻哑铃向胸上方受控推起，肘保持微屈。
actions.pose: Exercise pose: controlled LIGHT DUMBBELL INCLINE CHEST PRESS at upper push phase. A stable gray adjustable incline bench with backrest locked at 45 degrees to horizontal and a properly joined short seat. Woman reclines on it with head, upper back and hips SUPPORTED against the cushion, feet apart FLAT on the floor, no arched lower back or raised hips. Both hands securely hold matching small light gray dumbbells, one each. Hands pushed upwards above upper chest, arms angled up and slightly forward relative to reclined torso, elbows still gently flexed about 15–25 degrees, wrists straight and aligned with forearms. Dumbbells at about shoulder-width spacing, palms generally toward her feet in a comfortable press grip, not sideways fly and not vertical upright overhead seated shoulder press. Camera front three-quarter SIDE so bench incline, head support, both dumbbells, both arms and grounded feet are all clearly visible. Head rests naturally and face identity visible; look softly upward in direction of push. Frame whole bench and woman in portrait with natural body proportions.

actions.name: 单臂绳索或弹力带侧平举
actions.phase: 腰高固定锚点的单臂弹力带侧平举，动作臂抬至肩高以下。
actions.pose: Exercise pose: SINGLE-ARM resisted LATERAL RAISE with a correctly fixed WAIST-HEIGHT anchor, shown at controlled raised phase. Woman stands upright, chest faces camera with slight three-quarter turn showing original face. Feet hip-width apart flat on floor, torso level with no twist. A plain stable fixed gray vertical support pillar stands to her RIGHT side (left side of photograph), attachment eyelet is visibly at WAIST height. A lightly tensioned gray resistance band runs from this waist-height eyelet diagonally across IN FRONT of her lower torso to the handle held in her LEFT hand (farther from the anchor). She lifts that working LEFT arm out toward its own LEFT SIDE (right side of image), elbow softly bent, hand just BELOW shoulder level, arm not above shoulder, wrist neutral. Her nonworking right arm relaxed down beside body, not gripping the band. Band clearly connects anchor to working hand handle, no band ends floating and no bands at feet. She is lifting arm laterally in frontal plane, NOT raising forward, shrugging or rotating torso. Frame both shoulders, wrist, entire body, side pillar and waist-height connection so the pull direction is unmistakable.

actions.name: 站姿绳索或弹力带胸前飞鸟
actions.filename: 173_T-AXU-062_站姿绳索或弹力带胸前飞鸟.png
actions.phase: 双側略高于肩锚点，双臂前伸并保持轻屈肘，双手在上胸前接近会合。
actions.pose: Exercise pose: standing LIGHT CABLE CHEST FLY at near-converged front position. Woman upright in a stable short staggered stance, chest and face in front three-quarter view, shoulders relaxed, no backward lean. Two neutral-gray slim fixed upright posts of a minimalist cable crossover support stand to her sides SLIGHTLY BEHIND her body, one on each side. Each post has a visible small pulley anchor JUST ABOVE her shoulder height, with a thin cable running diagonally forward/down to a correctly constructed small gray handle in each hand. Exactly two cables and two separate handles, correctly attached, both anchors visibly above shoulders. Hands brought together IN FRONT OF MID-CHEST but still separated by about 10 cm, palms facing one another. Both arms form the smooth broad rounded arc of a hug: elbows stay gently bent about 15–25 degrees, away from body, not bent 90 degrees into a push. Shoulders and hips stay square, wrists neutral. Not overhead press, not overhead fly, not lying down, not pushing handles from bent elbows. Full woman, feet, arms, both thin posts and anchor-to-handle cable paths are visible. Original gray-blue studio backdrop and outfit remain unchanged.

corrections.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve, rehabilitation pose and equipment correction.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Images 2, 3, 4 lock the original woman's exact face, age, black low ponytail, white T-shirt, charcoal trousers, natural adult proportions, gray-blue mottled studio backdrop, floor and soft photographic lighting. Preserve the same woman and composition, stance, outfit, face and equipment style.
Correct the standing cable CHEST FLY pose and its shoulder-height pull geometry:
1. Move BOTH pulley/anchor centers down their gray upright posts to JUST ABOVE the woman's shoulder JOINTS, about 3–5 cm above shoulder level (in this framing near the upper-arm sleeve level, not above her head). Keep both posts and bases unchanged, pulleys securely mounted with correctly connected cable paths to each handle. The cable should travel almost horizontally slightly downward to her front chest-height hands, not steeply from far overhead.
2. Make the arms the gently curved rounded shape of a chest FLY ending in front, not a press with deeply bent elbows. BOTH elbow angles should be approximately 155–165 degrees (only 15–25 degrees of flexion), with upper arms and forearms nearly continuing each other. Hands in front of mid-chest about 10–15 cm apart, palms facing one another, wrists aligned. Arms extend forward in a broad gentle hug, elbows only slightly soft, NOT 90 degrees. Slightly more frontal view of the arm plane if needed to make the small elbow bends clearly visible; preserve the exact facial identity. Hand grips must look natural, with five fingers each and correctly joined handles.
Maintain shoulders lowered and trunk upright, short stable staggered stance. No other changes. Keep complete body and both shoes visible, the SAME gray-blue photographic background and lighting, portrait1122x1402. No words, arrows, inset, collage or extra people.

Image 1 is the edit target. Images 2, 3, 4 are the original exact-woman references. Preserve all identity, face, ponytail, white shirt, dark-gray trousers, normal adult body proportions, stable stance, shoes, corrected pulley heights and both gray posts, seamless pale gray-blue studio background and soft photographic lighting.
Change ONLY the arm pose to the END OF A STANDING CHEST FLY. Use the arm extension posture of original reference image 3 (woman reaching straight forwards) as the biomechanical guide, now for BOTH arms, except retain a small natural elbow softness and inward-facing grips. BOTH upper arms should be raised forward close to SHOULDER HEIGHT, rather than pointing down the sides of torso. Both upper arm and forearm axes almost line up: elbow flexion only 15–20 degrees, elbow inside angle 160–165 degrees. From shoulder to elbow to wrist, each arm must visually make one nearly straight forward-reaching line, NOT the bent-arm L shape of a chest press. Bring handles toward one another in front of UPPER CHEST, about 12cm apart, palms face inward, shoulders level and relaxed. Hold handles naturally and reconnect the cable paths to the existing corrected shoulder-level pulleys. Keep wrists neutral, no hand distortion. The forearms should NOT be horizontal while upper arms hang downward.
The endpoint is the gentle rounded end of a hugging fly, almost straight arms extended in front at upper-chest height. Single photorealistic continuous portrait1122x1402, complete body/feet/face, all other parts unchanged, no text, arrows, extra people, collage, inset or scene redesign.
